title: PFC Jones at the rotor head
description: A crewman in white T-shirt and cap — Larry believes this is PFC Jones — stands atop a Huey's fuselage working at the main rotor head, cigarette in mouth, silhouetted against a bright cumulus sky. At the far left edge, the tail fin of an adjacent aircraft carries a painted bird-like emblem. The flight line, Larry says, was "probably 3 blocks away," and a de Havilland Beaver was kept there.
researchNotes: Identification relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0012-c18035104.json and -c18035111.json), hedged as belief. Jones recurs: white-T-shirt crewman at the Huey in VN-0020, and possibly the owner of Sarge the monkey ('Jones, the helicopter pilot', VN-0017 comment). The painted tail emblem at frame left remains the strongest physical lead for the unit identification (unresolved question #2). Magnification pass 2026-08-15 (research/magnification/vn-0012-tail-emblem.png): the emblem is now resolved well enough to compare against documented 1964–65 unit tail art. The candidate readings are kept in research/magnification/README.md and are not summarized here while unconfirmed. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0012-c18415667.json and -c18415677.json): 'Location: Ton Son Nhut', the flight line 'probably 3 blocks away', and a Beaver there 'made by Canadian company Dehavolond'. The aircraft brought back a story that is not a caption for this frame: he flew to Hong Kong in another de Havilland, which he could not name at first and then called the Caribou ('Not sure on spelling') — two engines on the wings, short take-off and landing, popular for short strips, 'I think they held 18 guys.' His description fits the twin-engine de Havilland Canada DHC-4 Caribou, a short take-off transport the U.S. Army flew in Vietnam in this period; that a Caribou carried him to Hong Kong is his account and is not checked, and the trip is new to the archive. R&R flights from Vietnam to Hong Kong did exist: a Stars and Stripes item of 6 September 1965 reports their suspension (research/events/kia-misreport-stars-stripes.md). The Beaver is also drawn and labelled on his 2026-09-12 sheet of the airport (VD-0004).
